clue.text: The Spanish president almost backing fine for consumption

indicators.note: backing means the whole run of letters before it is read from the end to the start

parts.note: el is the Spanish for 'the'

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the president's name is left off

parts.note: Joe Biden, US president
the final letter of the name, dropped

explanation.surface: A Spanish president, apparently close to supporting a fine, all somehow about food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts BIDEN to BIDE; EL plus BIDE gives ELBIDE, and 'backing' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Something edible is safe and suitable to be eaten, which is what fine for consumption describes.

clue.text: Soused duke forced to give up whiskey

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for duke
WRENCHED (forced) losing W, which is whiskey in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A drunken duke is made to go without his whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soused' suggests the drunk duke of the surface, but here it means soaked through. Whiskey is W in the phonetic alphabet (Alpha, Bravo… Whiskey).
explanation.definitionFit: Soused can mean soaked in liquid, just as drenched does.

clue.text: Caravan getting an upgrade for the first time — enjoy the trip!

indicators.text: getting an upgrade for the first
indicators.note: an upgrade lifts a grade from C to B, and 'for the first' says only the opening letter is changed

parts.note: a caravan is a convoy, a group of vehicles or travellers moving together
the opening letter, treated as a grade
the grade one step up from C
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A caravan owner gets an upgrade for the first time and is wished a happy holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting an upgrade for the first' lifts CONVOY's opening C to B, giving BONVOY, and AGE follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: The French farewell is said to a traveller, wishing a good journey, the same as enjoy the trip.

clue.text: Symbol of love very touching, in retrospect

indicators.note: looking back, so the letters are read from the end

parts.note: so = very, as in 'so kind'
re = about, touching on

explanation.surface: Looking back, some token of love seems very moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touching' reads as moving, but here it means concerning, which is RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros, the Greek god of love, stands for love itself.

clue.text: Junction stops vehicle following gangster alongside Arizona prison

indicators.note: the junction plugs the middle of the vehicle, sitting inside it
Arizona sits next to the rest

parts.note: Al Capone, the crossword's usual gangster

indicators.note: the car comes after the gangster

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
a T-junction; T goes inside CAR to make CATR
AZ is the postal abbreviation for Arizona

explanation.surface: Traffic at a junction halts a mobster's car near an Arizona jail.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, Al Capone was himself imprisoned in Alcatraz.
explanation.definitionFit: Alcatraz was a notorious island prison in San Francisco Bay.

clue.text: A Catholic afterlife without hot or fun places

parts.note: taken as it stands
RC = Roman Catholic
HADES, the underworld, without H for hot

explanation.surface: A Catholic imagines a hereafter free of heat, or of any fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Or' misleads: it reads as a choice between hot and fun, but it ends the wordplay and joins it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: amusement arcades, full of slot machines and games, are one kind of place people go for fun.

clue.text: Criticisms about Platonism being misinterpreted

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: Platonism misinterpreted is read wrongly, so its letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Critics object that a philosophy has been misread.
explanation.definitionFit: Complaints are expressions of dissatisfaction, and criticisms are the same kind of grievance voiced aloud or in print.

clue.text: Almost all of cricket team getting Home Counties contract

indicators.note: getting means the first piece acquires the second, which is attached after it

parts.note: a cricket team has eleven players, so almost all of it is ten
the Home Counties around London lie in the South East of England, abbreviated SE

explanation.surface: Most of a cricket side signs a deal with clubs near London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London, all in England's South East.
explanation.definitionFit: To tense the muscles is to contract or tighten them, a verb sense rather than the legal one.

clue.text: Keys to auditorium passages

indicators.note: to an audience's ears: as it is heard

parts.note: keys are low islands, such as the Florida Keys; say the word for islands and hear a homophone

explanation.surface: The keys that open a theatre's passageways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keys' suggests unlocking doors, but it means small islands. The auditorium setting doubles as the sound signal and a place with aisles.
explanation.definitionFit: Aisles are the passages between rows of seats.

clue.text: More soldiers and frontiersmen violently besieging church

indicators.note: roughly handled, so the letters are thrown into a new order
surrounding: the letters go around the church

parts.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters
CE = Church of England, held inside the rearranged letters

explanation.surface: Troops and pioneers lay violent siege to a church.
explanation.walkthrough: The military surface hides that 'More soldiers' is the whole definition; the rest is letters to reorder with CE.
explanation.definitionFit: Reinforcements are extra soldiers sent to strengthen a force.

clue.text: Sound of allergic reaction from one half of train

parts.note: a = one, as in 'a dog'
a child's word for a train is CHOO-CHOO; half of it is CHOO

explanation.surface: Someone with hay fever sneezes in one of a train's carriages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' is the nursery choo-choo, not the railway carriage the surface implies.
explanation.definitionFit: Hay fever and other allergies set off sneezing, and this is how a sneeze is spelt in print.

clue.text: Sinner's rude tale about king

indicators.note: turned about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters
R = rex, Latin for king, added to the fodder

explanation.surface: A sinner tells a crude story about a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sinner's' reads as possessive, but it is 'Sinner is'. 'About' looks like 'concerning'; it shuffles all nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An adulterer commits a sin against marriage.

clue.text: In favour of Chinese native swallowing American government's political broadcast?

indicators.note: taking something inside, as the panda takes in GA

parts.note: pro = for, in favour of
the giant panda is native to China
G = government
A = American; GA goes inside PANDA: PA(GA)NDA

explanation.surface: A Chinese native backs an American state broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: The inserted letters come out as GA, government before American, the reverse of the clue's order. The question mark admits not every broadcast of this kind is propaganda.
explanation.definitionFit: Propaganda is political messaging spread to sway opinion.

clue.text: The woman's a goddess

parts.note: her = the woman's, belonging to her
taken as it stands

explanation.surface: A woman is declared divine.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as 'the woman is a goddess'; split it as HER + A instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Hera is the queen of the Greek gods.

clue.text: Second Conservative elected to infiltrate socialists withdraws

indicators.note: to get inside: the letters slip into the socialists

parts.note: reds = socialists
s = second, as in units
C = Conservative
a candidate elected is in

explanation.surface: A second Tory, once elected, is sent to spy on the left, and pulls out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Withdraws' could be read as the socialists retreating, but it is the definition: a verb, as when an offer is withdrawn.
explanation.definitionFit: To rescind a law or offer is to withdraw it.

clue.text: Sit with old man suffering problem with vision

indicators.note: in a bad way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder
anagram fodder, joined to SIT by 'with'

explanation.surface: A suffering old man sits down with poor eyesight.
explanation.walkthrough: The old man is not DAD or PA here; the words are taken letter by letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Daltonism is colour blindness, named after the chemist John Dalton, who had it.

clue.text: Eagle possibly dropping one across street in part of Germany

indicators.note: across means the remaining letters stretch over either side of the street abbreviation
dropping means the word one is taken away from the phrase

parts.note: in golf an eagle, two under par, on a par-three hole is a hole in one
the word itself, removed

explanation.surface: An eagle loses one bird as it flies over a road in a German region.
explanation.walkthrough: An eagle on a par-three is a hole in one; 'dropping one' leaves HOLEIN, which goes 'across' ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Holstein is a historic region of northern Germany, now joined with Schleswig as a federal state.

clue.text: Most tragic perhaps, Dominic Cummings' virtuous parts

definitions.meaning: the superlative of a slang word for a tear-jerking film, the kind that makes you cry
a jibe: his most pious (pi-est) parts are wee, tiny

explanation.surface: A political dig at Boris Johnson's adviser, whose saintly side is hard to find.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer as WEE PIEST: PI is slang for pious, so the piest bits are the most virtuous, and they are wee.
explanation.definitionFit: A weepie is a sad film; the weepiest is the most tragic of them.

clue.text: As hill next to point and line on map

indicators.note: 'next to' means adjacent, so the point's letter is set directly beside the As-plus-hill chunk, in front of it

parts.note: E = east, a compass point
qua = as, in the capacity of
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A map shows a hill beside a point and a line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As' reads as a mere connector, but it gives QUA, Latin for 'in the role of'.
explanation.definitionFit: The equator is the line drawn round the middle of the globe on maps.

clue.text: Play down the odd letters going missing in French city

indicators.note: letters 1, 3, 5 and 7 are dropped, leaving the even ones

parts.note: the eight letters of PLAYDOWN; strike out the 1st, 3rd, 5th and 7th (P, A, D, W)

explanation.surface: Some odd letters vanish in a French city, and it is hushed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play down' looks like the instruction, but it is the source of the letters: PlAyDoWn keeps L, Y, O, N.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyon is France's third-largest city.

clue.text: Plumb arcane quarters of the lower region

indicators.note: the answer lives in the words, housed inside them

parts.note: pLUMB ARcane

explanation.surface: Someone explores the mysterious regions of the underworld.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarters' suggests districts of the lower region, but it means lodgings: the answer is housed in the first two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumbar describes the lower back, the region below the ribs.

clue.text: Stick firmly to petition to keep every girl's clothing child-friendly

indicators.note: to hold the letters inside

parts.note: to sue is to petition a court
per = every, as in 'per day'

indicators.note: the outside of the word, its clothes

parts.note: the outer letters of GIRL
U is the British film rating meaning suitable for all ages

explanation.surface: A petition insists that all girls' clothes be safe for children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothing' does not mean garments here: a word's clothing is its outside, so only the first and last letters of 'girl' are used.
explanation.definitionFit: To superglue something is to stick it firmly with strong glue.

clue.text: And this, according to Virgil, is a rule to live by

indicators.note: in the words of a Roman poet, so in Latin

parts.note: et is Latin for and
hic is Latin for this

explanation.surface: A line from the Roman poet offering a motto for life.
explanation.walkthrough: Virgil stands for Latin: translate 'And this' word for word.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethic is a moral principle one lives by.

clue.text: Building hotel by river

indicators.note: beside: the river sits next to the hotel

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO alphabet
the Ouse is an English river, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A hotel is going up beside the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Building' reads as construction in progress, but it is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a house is one kind of building, the kind people live in.

clue.text: Find oneself before a king's magistrate

indicators.note: placed in front of the rest

parts.note: to find oneself somewhere is to be there
taken as it stands
K = king, in chess and cards

explanation.surface: Someone ends up in front of a royal judge.
explanation.walkthrough: Beak is British slang for a magistrate.
explanation.definitionFit: A British slang sense, originally thieves' cant, for a judge in a lower court.

clue.text: Old-fashioned, as Murdoch is?

definitions.meaning: Rupert Murdoch owns The Times newspaper, so he stands behind it

explanation.surface: A media mogul is mocked as out of date.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: Murdoch owns The Times of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone behind the times has not kept up with modern ways.

clue.text: Lay weapon before leader

indicators.note: placed in front of the leader

parts.note: an arm is a weapon, as in firearms
the chair leads a meeting

explanation.surface: Someone puts down a gun in front of their commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay' reads as a verb, set down; it is the adjective meaning amateur, as in an armchair critic.
explanation.definitionFit: Armchair describes someone with no professional experience, as a lay person has none.

clue.text: Lower-class ruffian retreats, having stolen my French gown

indicators.note: goes backwards, so the letters are read from the end

parts.note: oik is British slang for a lout
mon is French for my; it goes inside the reversed ruffian, after its second letter

explanation.surface: A thug runs off with a Frenchman's dressing gown.
explanation.walkthrough: An oik is a British term for a coarse, lower-class lout.
explanation.definitionFit: A kimono is a loose Japanese robe, often worn as a dressing gown.
